You can work hard and still feel stuck: too much advice, too many features, too little evidence, and nobody helping you question your own assumptions. The weight is real. You are allowed to need structure.
Discover helps you turn a broad idea into a specific customer problem and opportunity you can explain.
“I’m afraid of building the wrong thing.”
Validate helps you test risky assumptions before adding more features or committing more resources.
Build, Launch and Scale turn ambition into scoped work, measured learning and decisions about what comes next.

To turn “What do I do now?” into a manageable action: understand it, do the work, challenge it, and carry the result into the next lesson. Your worksheets become a venture record you can review and improve.
The Academy provides a learning structure. Customers, real-world testing and qualified support still matter. A completed worksheet is progress, not proof of demand or a promise of funding.
Every phase answers a founder question.
5 phases · 20 modules · 100 lessons. Each phase contains four modules of five lessons. Module 00 prepares you; it is separate from the 100 lessons.
Understand entrepreneurship, find opportunities, shape an idea and evaluate it. Carry a focused opportunity and your assumptions into Validate.
“What do customers and evidence tell me?”
Discover customers, understand the market, test the business model and decide whether to build. Carry findings, limits and unresolved conditions into Build.

Design and develop the product, establish the business and prepare for launch. Scope → essential features → user flow → build approach → prototype. Then test usability, define requirements and review readiness.
“How do I reach customers and learn?”
Prepare for market, build commercial systems, launch and learn, and measure traction. Use actual behaviour and results to improve your next decisions.
Build for growth, develop the organization, address capital and governance, and consider long-term venture strategy. Growth follows readiness and evidence; it is not automatic.
The sidebar shows every phase, module and lesson, plus your progress.
This is the same flow you will use inside the lessons. Module 00 lets you practise it before Lesson 01.
Review the storyboard/transcript or produced video when available.
Read the plain-language explanation, definitions and example.
Complete the interactive worksheet using your previous deliverable as input. Local autosave preserves your draft.
Use Teach Me, Guide Me, Review My Work or Challenge My Idea, or type a question. Current replies are simulated.
Answer the red-team questions. Separate assumptions from evidence and name what could change your decision.
Answer the quiz and review feedback. Built lessons require all three answers correct before completion.
Preview/export the deliverable, finish the checklist and explicitly self-complete. Carry the work into the next lesson. Reviewer submission is not connected.
“I don’t know yet” is useful when you name what you need to learn next. Narrowing scope or changing direction can be a strong founder decision.

orientationCoach.teach: Start with a customer problem: who experiences it, what happens, and what makes it costly or frustrating? Discover turns this into a focused opportunity.
orientationCoach.guide: Choose one next action: record a problem you have observed and the customer who experiences it. Begin Lesson 01, then follow the connected Discover lessons.
orientationCoach.review: For a useful self-review, check that your work names a customer, a task, evidence sources, assumptions and the next unanswered question. I have not inspected or approved your draft.
orientationCoach.challenge: What could make your idea unnecessary? How does the customer solve the problem now? Which assumption would change your decision if it were wrong?

It can feel heavy when every decision seems urgent. Make the next step smaller: write one customer problem, one unknown and one action you can take next. You can pause and return. The Academy gives structure; trusted peers or mentors can provide human support too.

Start with a problem you have seen firsthand. Name who faces it, what they do today and why it matters. If you have several ideas, record them before choosing one focused problem to explore in Discover. You do not need a perfect idea to begin Lesson 01.

Separate belief from evidence. In Validate, identify risky assumptions, speak with relevant customers and run bounded tests. Record what happened, what did not, and the limits. Interest alone is not proof of willingness to use or pay.

Use the Build sequence: scope one task, prioritize essential features and map its flow. Keep exclusions and dependencies visible. A prototype helps you test a question; it does not automatically establish demand or readiness.

This demo cannot assess funding, legal, medical or financial decisions. The curriculum includes capital, governance and planning topics, but a qualified person should review decisions using your actual circumstances. For now, write the decision, evidence needed and responsible reviewer.

I can accept your question, but this local scripted demo cannot give an open-ended answer to it. To move forward, name the decision you are making, what you know, what is uncertain and the next evidence you need. A connected production AI Coach will need a secure backend before it can respond to arbitrary questions.
